title: Tsunamis vs. Ocean Swim
description: Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Iwakuni’s elementary through high school swimmers compete against local Japanese schools in a swim meet at Iron Works Gym pool, MCAS Iwakuni, Japan, Feb. 16, 2020. This swim meet took place in order to foster a positive relationship between base residents and Japan through friendly competition and sport. (U.S. Marine Corps video by Pfc. Bryant Rodriguez)

transcript.text: (gentle funky music)
- My name is Kelly Wilkinson
and I'm the head coach of the Tsunami Swim Team
here at MCAS Iwakuni.
So today we had our home host meet
with the Ocean Swim Team, here locally in Iwakuni, Japan.
The overarching purpose, I think, for one,
is just foster our friendship with the local Iwakuni teams
and just youth sports, and then on top of that
just for some friendly competition
for the kids to test out their times.
I know our kids, we had an inter-squad meet two weeks ago
where our kids kinda raced each other
to prepare for this meet
and it's just really fun to race kids of new teams
and the Oceans team has some really fast kids
and we really enjoy swimming against them.
So both teams, I mean from a time standpoint,
did really well.
We have a lot of the Ocean swimmers
swam against us less than a year ago,
so we have all of their times in our computer system,
and so everyone did really well.
I mean, all of our kids dropped quite a bit of time
and the meet went really smoothly.
I think everyone had a lot of fun.
And, yeah, all the swimmers did great.
I mean, they dropped a lot of time.
So it was a really great day.
